candidates.title: Your camera says the Moon never grew
candidates.opening_promise: Same settings, same width: the Moon never grew.

thumbnail.concept: one big moon with an equal-width ruler under it

candidates.description: Photos taken with the same settings show the horizon Moon the same width as the high Moon. A leading explanation for the bigger look: your brain judges it farther away.
candidates.rationale: the measurement against what your eyes say

candidates.title: The giant horizon Moon isn't bigger
candidates.opening_promise: The giant Moon is actually a bit farther away.

thumbnail.concept: an eye looking at a big low moon along a distance line

candidates.description: At the horizon the Moon is about 1.5 percent farther from you than overhead, so it is very slightly smaller in the sky. The bigger look is an illusion.
candidates.rationale: the misconception, with a backwards-sounding fact on the cover

candidates.title: Your brain sees the horizon Moon bigger
candidates.opening_promise: The camera says same size. Your brain disagrees.

thumbnail.concept: a thinking brain beside a moon low on the horizon

candidates.description: A leading explanation: the brain judges the horizon Moon to be farther away, so it sees it as larger. Scientists still do not agree on the exact cause.
